questions.question: Where should hazardous materials shipping papers be placed?

options.text: At the bottom of a stack of shipping papers.
On the top of a stack of shipping papers.
In a separate location from non-hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the top of a stack of shipping papers.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials shipping papers must be on top so drivers and carriers can find them quickly.

questions.question: What class are flammable gases?
questions.explanation: Flammable gases are Class 2 hazardous materials.

questions.question: What does "RQ" mean?
questions.explanation: RQ stands for reportable quantity. You can use "RQ" instead of "X" on shipping papers when a reportable quantity of a hazardous material is being transported.

questions.question: Where should hazardous materials shipping papers be when the driver is not in the vehicle?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials shipping papers must always be easy to find. Leave them on the driver's seat when you leave the vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials?

options.text: Make sure no other vehicles are at the station.

questions.explanation: Always turn off the engine before refueling a vehicle with hazardous materials. Someone must stay at the nozzle and control the fuel flow at all times.

questions.question: When can you move a vehicle that is not properly placarded?

options.text: To make room for other vehicles.
If you are traveling less than 10 miles.

questions.explanation: A vehicle must have proper placards before driving. An improperly placarded vehicle can only be moved if it is necessary to protect people or property in an emergency.

questions.question: What is the best way to learn about hazardous materials transportation, in addition to reading the manual?
questions.explanation: The manual has information for the written test, but hazardous materials training courses teach you how to do the job safely.

questions.question: What should you do before opening trailer doors during a minor truck fire?

options.text: Feel the doors to see if they are hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel the doors to see if they are hot.
questions.explanation: Before opening trailer doors during a fire, feel them to check if they are hot. Hot doors mean there may be a cargo fire. Keep the doors closed if there is a cargo fire.

questions.question: What must you do when approaching a railroad crossing while transporting chlorine?

options.text: Slow down before crossing the tracks.
Proceed if no warning lights are flashing.
Proceed if no other vehicles are nearby.

questions.explanation: When transporting any amount of chlorine, you must always stop at a railroad crossing. Stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track.

questions.question: What should you do about restrictions on transporting explosives or hazardous waste?

options.text: They are usually not a concern.
They do not apply on weekends.
Research them before choosing your route.
They only apply if transporting more than 1,000 pounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Research them before choosing your route.
questions.explanation: Research any restrictions on your planned routes before transporting hazardous materials.

questions.question: When must you use a "Poison Inhalation Hazard" placard?

options.text: For any amount of the product.
Only when the container is leaking.

questions.correctAnswerText: For any amount of the product.
questions.explanation: You must display the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" placard and the hazard class placard at all times, no matter how small the amount.

questions.question: When loading hazardous materials, which should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: Do not use hooks or tools that could damage containers or packaging.

questions.question: What does a material's hazard class tell you?

options.text: The risks associated with the material.
Where items go on the trailer.
How to load and unload the material.

questions.correctAnswerText: The risks associated with the material.
questions.explanation: There are nine hazard classes. Each one identifies the risks of that material.

questions.question: What should a driver check about shipping papers?

options.text: They match the markings and labels on packages.
All packages are labeled as poison.
They are not in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: They match the markings and labels on packages.
questions.explanation: Compare the shipping paper to the package markings and labels. Make sure the basic description on the shipping paper matches what is on the packages.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, where should you NOT park?
questions.explanation: Never park a vehicle with Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. Also stay at least 5 feet from the road. Park only briefly when necessary.

questions.question: What is the minimum fire extinguisher rating for a placarded vehicle?
questions.explanation: The engine area must have a fire extinguisher with a UL rating of at least 10 B:C.

questions.question: If hazardous cargo is leaking, what should the driver do?

options.text: Drive to find a phone to call emergency personnel.
Drive to a hazardous materials cleanup facility.
Park the vehicle and call emergency personnel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park the vehicle and call emergency personnel.
questions.explanation: Stop the vehicle and do not drive longer than necessary. Continuing to drive spreads contamination. Park safely, secure the area, stay with the vehicle, and get help.

questions.question: How can you tell if a shipment may contain hazardous materials?

options.text: The shipper is in a business like fireworks or pest control.
Your last shipment was labeled as hazardous.
The shipper's location is in a bad area.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper is in a business like fireworks or pest control.
questions.explanation: If the shipper's business involves materials you would expect to be hazardous, the shipment may contain hazardous materials. Examples include paint dealers, chemical suppliers, and pest control firms.

questions.question: What shape are hazardous materials placards?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: What does "Forbidden" mean in the Hazardous Materials Table?

options.text: The substance must be transported by air.
The substance can only be transported at night.
The substance must be accompanied by a security guard.

questions.explanation: Never transport any material marked "Forbidden" in the Hazardous Materials Table.

questions.question: If a vehicle carrying Class 1 explosives is in a collision, what should the driver do?

options.text: Not warn others about the danger.
Keep the explosives in the vehicle until after moving the vehicles apart.
Remove the explosives from the vehicle before moving the vehicles apart.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove the explosives from the vehicle before moving the vehicles apart.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle carrying Class 1 explosives is in a collision, warn others of danger, keep people away, and do not allow smoking or open flames near the vehicle. Remove all explosives and place them at least 200 feet away from the vehicles and any buildings.

questions.question: If hazardous materials cargo catches fire while you are transporting it, what should you do?

options.text: Try to put out the fire with a fire extinguisher.
Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
Wait and hope the fire goes out on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
questions.explanation: Fighting a hazardous materials fire requires special training and protective equipment. Do not try to fight this type of fire yourself unless you have proper training and equipment.

questions.question: What must a shipping paper generally list?

options.text: The location of fire departments along your route.

questions.explanation: Shippers must list an emergency response telephone number on hazardous materials shipping papers. Some exceptions to this rule may apply.

questions.question: What is the only way to check tire pressure correctly?

options.text: Push on the tires to feel the pressure.

questions.explanation: Check each tire at the start of each trip. Using a tire pressure gauge is the only effective way to check tire pressure.

questions.question: A person watching the loading or unloading of a tank must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Stay within 25 feet of the tank.
Know the hazards of the materials.

questions.explanation: The supervisor watching a cargo tank must stay alert, have a clear view of the tank, stay within 25 feet, know the material hazards, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: If a package is too small for a hazardous materials label, how should it be labeled?
questions.explanation: If a hazardous materials package is too small for a label, attach the label to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: When transporting packages of radioactive materials, what is important to know?

options.text: Radiation will pass through to other nearby packages.
The packages must be carried in the cab.
The packages must be loaded on their side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation will pass through to other nearby packages.
questions.explanation: Radiation surrounds radioactive material packages and passes through to other packages nearby. Because of this, there are limits on how many radioactive packages can be loaded together.

questions.question: Who is responsible for placing placards on a vehicle?
questions.explanation: The shipper provides the placards, but the driver is responsible for actually placing them on the vehicle.

questions.question: How should a shipper tell a driver about cargo risks?

options.text: By writing a note on a blank piece of paper.
By placing hazard warning labels on packages.
By placing orange dots on packages.

questions.correctAnswerText: By placing hazard warning labels on packages.
questions.explanation: Shippers must alert drivers and others to hazards using shipping papers, hazard warning labels on packages, emergency response information, and placards.

questions.question: What is a Class 7 hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Class 7 hazardous materials are radioactive materials.
